files.lesson.md: --- order: 42 unit: conditional10 node: AC9M10P01 n1 uses: [AC9M9P02 n2, AC9M8P02 n1] # and / or from a Venn diagram; a two-way table connection: chance-of-rain title: Given summary: "'The chance of rain, given a cloudy morning' is a chance inside a smaller group. Say which event is known, which is asked about, and why swapping them changes the answer." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The sky is grey this morning. Should that change what you say about the chance of rain this afternoon?" explainPicture: { ref: rain.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Given a cloudy morning, only the 50 cloudy days count. Rain fell on 30 of them, so the chance is 30 out of 50." } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8440 url: http://127.0.0.1:8440/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- A forecast chance of rain is the likelihood of more than the smallest rainfall a gauge can measure, 0.2 mm ([Interpreting BOM forecasts, FarmPoint](https://farmpoint.tas.gov.au/news/interpreting-bom-forecasts), checked 22 October 2026). A forecaster also knows things about the morning. This lesson uses 100 spring days in a town. The numbers are made up. Every day is sorted by two questions: did it rain, and was the morning cloudy? ## Predict: which way round ```step stage: predict insight: "The same 30 days sit inside both groups, so many students expect the two chances to match. A chance given a group is found inside that group, and the groups have different sizes." check: type: predict q: "Look at the picture. Rain fell on 40 of the 100 days and 50 mornings were cloudy; 30 days had both. Which is bigger: the chance of rain, given a cloudy morning, or the chance of a cloudy morning, given rain?" options: - "Rain given cloudy is bigger" - "Cloudy given rain is bigger" - "They are equal, because both use the same 30 days" actual: "Cloudy given rain is bigger. Given rain, look at the 40 rainy days: 30 of them had a cloudy morning, which is 30/40 = 0.75. Given a cloudy morning, look at the 50 cloudy days: 30 of them had rain, 30/50 = 0.6." ``` Make a guess before you use the board. ## Run: only the cloudy mornings ```step stage: run insight: "'Given a cloudy morning' shrinks the whole to the 50 cloudy days. The days outside it fade, because knowing the morning was cloudy rules them out. The chance is the chosen part over that smaller whole." try: { playground: board, starter: "rain.yml#run", height: 640 } check: { type: board, text: "The board is set to 'given cloudy'. Choose the rain parts (Rain only and Rain and Cloudy) and read the chance. Then switch Rain only off and on to see which parts count. What is the chance of rain, given a cloudy morning?", when: "g = 50 and h = 30" } ``` The words after "given" say what you know. Everything that does not fit is left out, so the whole is no longer the 100 days. It is the 50 cloudy ones. ## Investigate: which group do you look at ```step stage: investigate insight: "In 'chance of A, given B' you look inside B and ask how much of B is also A. Swapping the two events changes the group you look in, so the chance changes too." tasks: - check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "In a survey of 50 students (made up), 30 play basketball, 20 play volleyball and 8 play both. What is the chance a student plays volleyball, given that they play basketball? Give a decimal to 2 places." steps: - ["Given basketball: the group is the 30 basketball players", "the given event picks the group"] - ["8 of those 30 also play volleyball", "count the 'both' students inside the group"] - ["$8 \\div 30 = 0.27$", "the part over the group"] answer: "0.27" answerLabel: "Chance" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["0.16", "That is 8 out of all 50 students. Given basketball, divide by the 30 who play it."] - ["0.4", "That is 8 out of 20, the chance of basketball given volleyball. Check which group the question gives."] criteria: - "I named the group first (the basketball players)." - "I counted the volleyball players only inside that group." - "I divided by the size of the group, not by 50." explain: "The group is the 30 basketball players, and 8 of them also play volleyball: 8 ÷ 30 = 0.27." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Given basketball means you look only at the basketball players. How many of the 50 students is that?", answer: 30, tolerance: 0, explain: "30 students play basketball. That is the whole you divide by." } - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ravi" text: "Ravi finds the chance of a cloudy morning, given that it rained. Click the line where he goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: conditional-direction-swapped explain: "Line 3: the thing given is rain, so he should look at the 40 days with rain, not the 50 cloudy mornings. 30 ÷ 40 = 0.75. He answered the question for the other direction." - check: type: question q: "'The chance a student plays sport, knowing that they walk to school.' Which group do you look inside?" options: ["The students who walk to school", "The students who play sport", "All the students", "The students who do both"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The sport players are what you count inside the group, not the group.", "'Knowing that' shrinks the whole to the walkers.", "The 'both' students are the ones you count, not the group."] explain: "'Knowing that they walk' is the given part, so you look at the walkers and ask how many of them play sport." ``` ### Two ways to say it In this lesson $P(\text{rain} \mid \text{cloudy})$ is read "the chance of rain, given a cloudy morning". Words such as "given", "if", "knowing that" and "of the" all do the same job: they point at the group you look in. ```worked P(\text{bike} \mid \text{scooter}) :: In a survey of 40 students (made up), 24 own a bike, 16 own a scooter and 10 own both. Read "given scooter": the scooter owners are the group. 10 \text{ of the } 16 \text{ scooter owners also own a bike} :: Count the students with both, but only inside that group. P(\text{bike} \mid \text{scooter}) = \tfrac{10}{16} = \tfrac{5}{8} :: The part over the group. P(\text{scooter} \mid \text{bike}) = \tfrac{10}{24} = \tfrac{5}{12} :: Swap the words and the group changes to the 24 bike owners, so the answer changes. ``` Now try one on paper first, with the example beside you. In a different survey (made up), 50 students were asked about two sports. Then type your answer. ### Find the mistake Read Ravi's working. Which line chooses the wrong group? ### Reading the sentence Pick the group first, then count. ## Modify: change what is given ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the given group changes the whole and so the chance. At the edge, a given group with nothing in it leaves no chance to work out." try: { playground: board, starter: "rain.yml#run", height: 640 } tasks: - starter: "rain.yml#clear" hint: ["The board is given 'not cloudy', the clear mornings. Choose the Rain parts.", "Only the Rain only part is inside the clear mornings."] check: { type: board, text: "Now the morning was clear. Choose rain and read the chance of rain, given a clear morning.", when: "g = 50 and h = 10", explain: "Of the 50 clear mornings, 10 had rain: 10/50 = 0.2." } - starter: "rain.yml#rainy" hint: "The group is the 40 rainy days. Choose the Cloudy parts." check: { type: board, text: "Now it is given that it rained. Choose cloudy and read the chance of a cloudy morning, given rain.", when: "g = 40 and h = 30", explain: "Of the 40 rainy days, 30 had a cloudy morning: 30/40 = 0.75." } - starter: "rain.yml#nodry" check: type: question q: "Edge case: in this board no day has rain (the Rain circle is empty). The board is given rain. What does it say about the chance of a cloudy morning, given rain?" options: ["It has no value: there are no rainy days to look at, so there is nothing to divide", "It is 0, because nothing happened", "It is 1, because cloudy is the only option", "It is 20 out of 100"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A chance of 0 would mean there were rainy days and none of them was cloudy.", "A chance of 1 would mean every rainy day was cloudy, and there are none.", "That is the share of days that were cloudy only, out of all 100. Given rain, the whole is empty."] explain: "With 0 rainy days there is no group to look in, so 'given rain' has no chance. The board says it is not defined." ``` ### Clear morning ### Given rain ### Nothing to look at ## Practise: reading and finding ```step stage: practise insight: "Finding a chance given a group from a table, then a review of and / or from Year 9." tasks: - check: { type: number, q: "Of the 100 days, 40 had a clear morning and, of those, 8 had rain (made up). What is the chance of rain, given a clear morning? Give a decimal.", answer: 0.2, tolerance: 0.01, feedback: [[0.08, "That is 8 out of all 100 days. Given a clear morning, the whole is the 40 clear mornings."]], explain: "8 ÷ 40 = 0.2." } - check: { type: number, q: "In a class of 30, 18 play netball, 12 play hockey and 6 play both (made up). What is P(hockey | netball), as a decimal?", answer: 0.33, tolerance: 0.01, feedback: [[0.5, "That is P(netball | hockey), 6 out of the 12 hockey players. Given netball, look at the 18 netball players."]], explain: "Given netball, the group is 18 students and 6 also play hockey: 6 ÷ 18 = 0.33." } - check: { type: number, q: "Review: use the 100 spring days (10 rain only, 30 both, 20 cloudy only, 40 neither). What is P(rain or cloudy)? Give a decimal.", answer: 0.6, tolerance: 0.01, feedback: [[0.5, "That counts only the cloudy days. 'Or' includes rain days as well."], [1.2, "40 + 50 counts the 30 days with both twice."]], explain: "10 + 30 + 20 = 60 of 100 days had rain or a cloudy morning: 0.6." } ``` ### Clear mornings ### Hockey given netball ### A review From Year 9: "or" takes everything in either group, and the overlap is counted once. That chance is not given anything, so the whole stays the 100 days. ## Make: back to the forecast ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the opening: a cloudy morning lets you say something more exact than the chance of rain on any day. A good report names the given group and compares the two chances." tasks: - check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "On any day in this town the chance of rain is $\\frac{40}{100} = 0.4$. A cloudy morning arrives. Using the table, what chance of rain would you give for that afternoon? (Decimal.)" steps: - ["Given a cloudy morning, the group is the 50 cloudy days", "the given event picks the group"] - ["30 of those 50 days had rain", "count the rain days inside the group"] - ["$30 \\div 50 = 0.6$", "the part over the group"] answer: "0.6" answerLabel: "Chance of rain" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["0.3", "That is 30 out of all 100 days. Given a cloudy morning, divide by the 50 cloudy mornings."] - ["0.4", "That is the chance on any day. The cloudy morning is something you know, so use it."] criteria: - "I named the group the 'given' picks." - "I counted rain only inside that group." - "I wrote the answer as a chance with the words 'given a cloudy morning'." explain: "0.6. Of the 50 cloudy mornings, 30 had rain. That is higher than the 0.4 for any day, because a cloudy morning is a clue." - check: type: question q: "Which sentence says what the table shows?" options: ["On days with a cloudy morning it rained on 3 in 5, but on all days it rained on 2 in 5", "It rained on 3 in 5 days", "A cloudy morning makes rain certain", "A cloudy morning has nothing to do with rain"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "3 in 5 is only for days with a cloudy morning. Say which days.", "3 in 5 is a long way from certain.", "0.6 against 0.4 shows that cloudy mornings and rain go together a little."] explain: "A conditional chance always needs its group: 0.6 given a cloudy morning, 0.4 on any day." ``` ### The forecast Work this out on paper first, then type your answer. ### What the table says Sources: the meaning of "chance of rain" is from [FarmPoint](https://farmpoint.tas.gov.au/news/interpreting-bom-forecasts) (checked 22 October 2026). The 100 days, the cloudy mornings and the rain counts, and the bike, scooter and sport counts, are made up for this lesson. **Also used in** - **Medicine.** A positive test result is a clue, and the chance of having the condition, given a positive result, is not the chance the test is right. - **Sport.** The chance a team wins, given it scores first, is looked up inside the games where it scored first. - **Next lesson.** Tables, Venn diagrams and trees all read the same conditional chance. ```teacher summary: Students read 'given', 'if … then' and 'knowing that' as pointing at a smaller group, and find the chance inside it. They see that P(rain | cloudy) and P(cloudy | rain) use different groups. The context is 100 made-up spring days sorted by rain and cloudy mornings (AC9M10P01, node 1). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can say which event is given and which is asked about. - I can find a chance inside the group the 'given' picks. - I can say why P(A | B) and P(B | A) are usually different. struggle: "Dividing by all the days instead of the group. Ask: 'Given what? Which days are left once you know that?'" before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need and / or from a Venn diagram (Year 9) and a two-way table. The one idea: "given" shrinks the whole to one group. Everything else is a count inside that group. The Venn board fades the days outside the group and says "of the g in the group, h are chosen". The notation P(A | B) is introduced here as a way of writing the words; it is not a formula. The language forms to put side by side: "given", "if … then", "knowing that", "of the". 'Of' is the odd one out: "of the cloudy mornings, how many had rain" is the same as "given a cloudy morning". Every count is made up: the 100 days, the cloudy mornings, the bike, scooter, sport and netball counts. The one real fact is what a forecast chance of rain means (more than the gauge's smallest measurable rainfall, 0.2 mm), from FarmPoint. This matters for the opening: the 0.4 here is a count from the town's days, not a forecast. running: - "Predict: show of hands. Many choose 'equal' because the 30 days appear in both." - "Run: ask students to say the group out loud before they read the board." - "Paper: the sport try-one and the forecast Make are worked on paper first. Look for the group named in the first line." - "Modify: before the empty board, ask 'if no day had rain, which days would you look at?'" stuck: - see: A student divides by 100 whatever the question says. ask: Once you know it was cloudy, which days are still possible? fix: Cross out the days that do not fit the given, then count what is left. - see: A student says P(rain | cloudy) and P(cloudy | rain) are the same because the same 30 days are in both. ask: What is the group in each? How big is each group? fix: "Same top, different bottom: 30/50 and 30/40." - see: A student reads 'given' as 'and' and answers 0.3. ask: Is that out of all the days or only the cloudy ones? fix: "'And' keeps the whole at 100. 'Given' shrinks the whole to the group." stretch: A test can give a result called 'positive' for people who do and do not have a condition. Say in words what 'the chance of a positive test, given the person has the condition' and 'the chance of having the condition, given a positive test' mean. Which one would you want a doctor to tell you? support: A printed Venn diagram and table. The student shades the given group first and crosses out the rest. leads: > Continues AC9M10P01 node 1. Where it leads: reading conditional chances from tables, Venn diagrams and trees (next lesson), and deciding whether two events are independent. exit: q: Of 60 students, 24 play football and 9 play football and tennis. What is the chance a football player plays tennis? What is the chance a tennis player plays football if 18 play tennis? a: 9/24 = 0.375, then 9/18 = 0.5. The group changes, so the answer changes. explain: > A chance "given" something is found inside the group where that thing is true. - Spot the given: "given", "knowing that", "if … then" and "of the" point at the group. - Shrink the whole: only the days or people in that group are counted. - Divide: count what you want inside the group, then divide by the size of the group. - Swapping the events changes the group, so P(A | B) is usually not P(B | A). sources: - title: "Interpreting BOM forecasts (FarmPoint, Tasmanian Government): chance of rain is the likelihood of more than the minimum measurable rainfall (0.2 mm)" url: https://farmpoint.tas.gov.au/news/interpreting-bom-forecasts checked: 2026-10-22 - title: "Made up for this lesson: the 100 days with their rain and cloudy-morning counts, and the bike, scooter, netball and sport counts." url: https://tutorials.learningwaypoints.com/maths/data/given/ checked: 2026-10-25 ```

# Boards for "Given". A town's 100 spring days (made up), sorted by two yes/no questions: did it rain that day (A), and was
# the morning cloudy (B). Counts are in the order: rain only (clear morning), both, cloudy only (dry day), neither.
# `given:` shrinks the whole to one group, so the board reads "of the g in the group, h are chosen".

# region: run
widget: venn
labels: Rain, Cloudy
counts: 10, 30, 20, 40
given: b
# endregion

# region: clear
widget: venn
labels: Rain, Cloudy
counts: 10, 30, 20, 40
given: not b
# endregion

# region: rainy
widget: venn
labels: Rain, Cloudy
counts: 10, 30, 20, 40
given: a
# endregion

# region: nodry
widget: venn
labels: Rain, Cloudy
counts: 0, 0, 20, 80
given: a
event: b
# endregion

# region: explain-pic
widget: venn
labels: Rain, Cloudy
counts: 10, 30, 20, 40
given: b
event: a
choose: off
# endregion
files.working.txt:
# Ravi's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: ravi
The question: what is the chance of a cloudy morning, given that it rained?
The days with both rain and a cloudy morning: 30.
"Given" means I look at the cloudy mornings, which is 50 days.
30 ÷ 50 = 0.6.
So the chance of a cloudy morning, given rain, is 0.6.
# endregion
